evidence.detail: get_recent_matches() and related functions return SQLAlchemy ORM queries with lazy-loaded relationships: players (via match_players secondary), modules, games, format, tournament — each will cause N+1 queries when rendered
paginate() call issues both a COUNT(*) query and the main query; combined with lazy-loading of 5 relationships per match row, this multiplies DB round-trips
Only one index migration exists in logsite history (on tournament.name), suggesting match/player join tables lack covering indexes

triage.notes: Cannot benchmark without a running server, but the ORM patterns (no selectinload/joinedload on players/games relationships, per-match lazy loading) are well-known sources of N+1 slowness. A proper fix requires profiling to identify the hottest queries, adding SQLAlchemy eager-loading options, and possibly adding DB indexes on match_players(match_id).
